Short Hypothesis: We advance three separable claims. (C1, phenomenon) When an interpretable SAE feature is steered to improve a target property (logP, QED, docking, a functional group) of a generated molecule, generation drifts systematically—not randomly—toward less synthesizable chemical space; this 'synthesizability tax' has a measurable dose-response and same-sign structure across features. (C2, blind spot) Standard output-side checks a practitioner actually runs (RDKit validity, property-predictor confidence, generation log-likelihood) carry near-zero information about this tax, so the manufacturability loss is invisible to normal evaluation. (C3, mechanism) Synthesizability is linearly decodable from activations yet, under the intervention families we test, we do NOT find a robust direction that steers it the way logP/QED can—i.e., it behaves as a decodable-but-weakly-steerable global property. We deliberately scope C3 as 'no robust steerable direction found under tested interventions,' not a universal absence claim.
Related Work: Synthesizability is 'the elephant in the lab': generative models routinely propose unmakeable molecules, addressed via post-hoc filtering (RAscore 2021, RetroGNN 2020), retrosynthesis-constrained generation (building-block assembly 2023, TANGO 2024, steerable synthesizability control 2025, SynTwins 2025), and retrosynthesis-in-the-loop optimization (2024). These are architecture/objective interventions treating synthesizability as an external constraint on the MODEL. A second line—molecular-LM interpretability (SynFlowNet interpretability 2025, 'Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers' 2025, token-level KL importance 2025)—shows physicochemical properties are linearly decodable and steerable. A third, general-interpretability line studies decodability-vs-causality: a probe reading a concept does not imply an intervention can steer it (activation patching, difference-of-means steering, SAE feature ablation). Positioning as a three-row contrast: (i) synthesizability-control papers CHANGE the model to make it steerable—we FREEZE the model and ask what interpretable steering costs; (ii) molecular-LM steering papers steer desired properties but never audit the synthesizability side-effect nor test synthesizability's own steerability; (iii) decodability-vs-causality papers give our diagnostic frame but were not applied to a chemical global property with real manufacturing stakes. No prior work quantifies a property-vs-synthesizability tradeoff induced by interpretable-feature steering, tests synthesizability's causal steerability head-to-head against physicochemical properties at matched decodability, or ships a reusable audit for it. Our contribution is thus threefold and clearly typed: a new empirical phenomenon (C1), a mechanistic diagnosis (C3), and a released audit/benchmark protocol—not a new generation method.
Abstract: Generative molecular design has a notorious blind spot: models propose molecules that cannot be made, 'the elephant in the lab.' The field fights this with retrosynthesis filters and synthesis-constrained generation, but no one has asked what happens to synthesizability when practitioners use the increasingly popular interpretable-feature steering to hit a target property. We surface and explain a phenomenon we call the synthesizability tax: steering an interpretable SAE feature to improve a desired property (logP, QED, docking, a functional group) systematically drags generation into less synthesizable chemical space, and the property-focused evaluations practitioners run never see it. We make three separable, pre-registered claims: (C1) the tax is systematic with a dose-response, not generic drift; (C2) cheap output-side checks are near-blind to it; and (C3) synthesizability is linearly decodable from activations yet, under all intervention families we test, has no robust steerable direction—unlike logP/QED at matched decodability. Using frozen autoregressive SMILES chemical language models with sparse autoencoders and cheap synthesizability oracles (SAscore, RAscore) validated against a retrosynthesis planner (AiZynthFinder route-found rate and route length) on stratified subsets, we quantify the tax with per-property normalized effect sizes; separate it from off-distribution drift using non-interpretable latent-steering, KL-matched, and temperature controls; test synthesizability's steerability head-to-head against physicochemical properties; and evaluate an orthogonalization mitigation with a pre-set success bar. Deliverable: an open audit suite that flags unmakeable steered designs before expensive retrosynthesis. Either outcome is actionable—a real tax changes steering evaluation protocols; a null result certifies interpretable steering as synthesizability-safe.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Model: a GPT-style autoregressive SMILES chemical language model, either public (MolGPT, ~6M) or trained by us (~15M, 8 layers, d=512) on ZINC-250k (249,455 molecules; 80/10/10 split by scaffold to prevent leakage). Base model FROZEN; only inference-time steering vectors added. Directions from TopK sparse autoencoders (over-complete dictionary reconstructing the residual stream with top-k active latents): expansion 16x, k=32, trained on 30M mid-layer residual vectors (layer picked by max intrinsic dimension; one alternative layer kept), Adam lr 3e-4, batch 4096, seeds 0/1/2. Steering = add alpha*d_hat to the residual during decoding; alpha in {0,1,2,4,8,16} residual-RMS units. Oracles (RDKit): logP, QED, MW, ring count (PROPERTY); SAscore (0-10, higher=harder), RAscore (0-1) (SYNTHESIZABILITY). ANTI-CIRCULARITY: features are discovered/selected on the train split only; tax and steerability are measured on held-out test generations. ORACLE VALIDATION as a primary result, not a footnote: on 3,000 stratified molecules run AiZynthFinder; require route-found rate and route length to track SAscore/RAscore (Spearman |rho|>=0.5) before any strong claim; report route-found rate as the ground-truth synthesizability signal alongside the cheap oracles throughout.

Experiment 1 (C1 - systematic, not random, and not generic drift): For 30-50 property-steering features (top by train-split property-probe AUROC), each (feature,alpha,seed) generates 500 valid molecules; measure target-property gain and Delta-SAscore/Delta-route-found vs alpha=0. DRIFT CONTROLS (all matched to the property-steering KL at each alpha): (a) random-direction, (b) matched non-property SAE feature, (c) non-interpretable raw-latent steering (PCA/difference-of-means on activations), (d) decoding-temperature perturbation. Decisive metric FIRST: per-property NORMALIZED tax slope beta* = d(z-scored SAscore)/d(z-scored target-property), from a mixed-effects model with random slopes over features/seeds, computed per property then pooled. Decision band (pre-set): pooled beta* >= +0.30 (95% CI excludes 0) AND same-sign for >=80% of features AND exceeding every KL-matched control by >=2x => systematic tax confirmed; beta* in [-0.10,+0.10] or CI crossing 0 => not established; beta* <= -0.10 => steering is synthesizability-SAFE (clean counter-result).

Experiment 2 (C2 - blind spot): Using Experiment-1 generations, test whether the cheap checks a practitioner runs reveal 'synthesizability cliffs' (RAscore crossing below 0.5, SAscore jump >=1.0, or route lost). Detectors: RDKit validity, property-predictor confidence, generation log-likelihood. Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between each check and the true SAscore/route drop. Decision band: |rho|<=0.20 for validity and property-confidence => blind spot confirmed; (0.20,0.40) => partial visibility; >=0.40 => not a blind spot.

Experiment 3 (C3 - decodable but no robust steerable direction): Data: 20,000 held-out molecules labeled by SAscore/RAscore and logP/QED. (a) DECODABILITY: ridge probe (5-fold CV) for each target from SAE features and raw activations (R^2/AUROC). (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: best synthesizability direction (probe-weight, difference-of-means high-vs-low, activation-patching from synthesizable runs) vs best logP and QED directions; steer each and measure on-target effect (Cohen's d of oracle value at the alpha maximizing on-target change within the validity budget). SCAFFOLD HELD FIXED operationalized: condition generation on a fixed Bemis-Murcko scaffold prefix (prompt the SMILES with the scaffold tokens), steer only the completion, and compare steered vs unsteered completions of the SAME scaffold (paired). Decisive metric FIRST: steerability ratio r = d(synthesizability)/median(d(logP),d(QED)) at matched decodability. Decision band: probe R^2>=0.50 AND r<=0.33 across >=2/3 direction types => C3 confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial; r>=0.67 with a working direction => synthesizability IS steerable (refutes C3, equally publishable).

Experiment 4 (mitigation, with a pre-set bar): orthogonalize each property-steering vector against the best (weak) synthesizability direction; SUCCESS iff it removes >=50% of the tax (beta* reduction) while retaining >=80% of the on-target property gain. Failure modes reported: if no usable synthesizability direction exists, orthogonalization is undefined and we say so.

ABLATIONS (PRIMARY, not optional): SMILES vs SELFIES, alternative SAE layer, SAE sparsity/width, model size (6M/15M/40M), oracle choice. A finding 'counts' only where it holds on >=2 axes. DELIVERABLE: release the labeled steered-generation set, the audit code (property-vs-synthesizability tradeoff + cliff detector), and per-property tax slopes as a reusable benchmark.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) SAscore/RAscore are in-silico proxies; we now elevate AiZynthFinder route-found rate/route length to a PRIMARY signal on stratified subsets and gate strong claims on cheap-vs-planner agreement. Claims concern model-internal, planner-verified manufacturability, not wet-lab synthesis. 2) C3 is scoped as an absence-under-tested-interventions claim, not a universal one; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types, sweeping strength, and head-to-head calibrating that PROPERTY features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive steerable synthesizability handle is equally publishable and directly useful. 3) The tax could be generic off-distribution drift; we use random, matched-non-property, non-interpretable-latent, KL-matched, and temperature controls, requiring the tax to exceed all KL-matched controls. 4) SAE quality/layer could confound Location and the tax; controlled via multiple SAE variants, layers, sparsity/width, and difference-of-means baselines as primary ablations. 5) Feature selection could induce circularity; we separate feature discovery (train split) from tax/steerability evaluation (test split). 6) Property targets are heterogeneous; we use per-property normalized (z-scored) tax slopes rather than a single raw threshold. 7) An internal synthesizability probe might not beat a raw-activation probe on AUROC; even so, the interpretability diagnosis (decodable-but-not-steerable) and the audit/mitigation payoff are the contributions. 8) A null tax is a valuable positive result: it certifies interpretable steering as synthesizability-safe and gives practitioners a clear go-ahead.

Name: interpretable_feature_bayesopt
Title: Optimizing in Concept Space: Do Interpretable SAE Features Make Scientific Design Optimization More Sample-Efficient and Auditable?
Short Hypothesis: Primary contribution: SAE-feature-space Bayesian optimization (BO) with a causal test of monosemanticity. We claim that running query-efficient BO with uncertainty (a Gaussian-process surrogate, not manual or greedy latent steering) directly over the sparse, monosemantic feature space of a sparse autoencoder trained on a frozen scientific foundation model yields more sample-efficient design than BO over the model's raw embeddings or a VAE latent, tested in two concrete settings: protein fitness optimization (ProteinGym/FLIP oracles) and small-molecule property optimization (penalized-logP, QED, docking). We further hypothesize that the per-dimension monosemanticity of the search space—defined quantitatively and pre-registered, not merely its dimensionality—causally predicts optimization efficiency, and that interpretability additionally enables concept-prior warm-starting and faithful, human-readable design trajectories that let a protein engineer choosing the next wet-lab construct see why each step was taken.
Related Work: Latent-space Bayesian optimization (LSBO) is a mature line: Automatic Chemical Design (Gomez-Bombarelli 2018), Constrained BO in VAE latent space (Griffiths & Hernandez-Lobato 2019), LaMBO (Stanton 2022), CLaSMO (2024), and low-dimensional semi-supervised latent BO for antimicrobial peptides (2025). Separately, SAE-steering work (InterPLM 2024, ProtSAE 2025, 'SAEs for Low-N Protein Function Prediction and Design' 2025, Steering Protein LMs/ASPO 2025) shows SAE latents can steer generation and even design high-fitness variants via manual latent steering. The crucial gap: (i) no prior work uses the INTERPRETABLE SAE feature space of a FROZEN foundation model as the actual optimization search space for closed-loop, oracle-guided Bayesian optimization; existing LSBO uses black-box VAE/embedding spaces, and the low-N SAE paper uses manual/greedy steering, not query-efficient BO with uncertainty. (ii) No one has tested whether the MONOSEMANTICITY of the search space is causally responsible for optimization efficiency, versus mere dimensionality reduction. (iii) No one exploits interpretability to warm-start BO with concept-property priors or to emit human-readable design trajectories. Our proposal isolates the value of interpretability as a search-space property, distinguishing it from generic dimensionality reduction, and from all prior LSBO and SAE-steering work. We further separate the interpretable-space claim from generic BO machinery by comparing against trust-region (TuRBO) and active-subspace BO run in every candidate space, and we validate on at least one real measured fitness landscape (ProteinGym/FLIP) rather than proxy oracles alone, so the efficiency claim is not an artifact of a particular optimizer or a synthetic oracle.
Abstract: Scientific design—of proteins, molecules, and sequences—is a query-efficiency problem: each oracle evaluation (an assay, a docking run, a simulation) is expensive, so the geometry of the search space decides how many experiments a designer must run. Latent-space Bayesian optimization (LSBO) searches the black-box latent of a task-specific VAE, while interpretability work shows sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose frozen foundation-model activations into monosemantic, concept-aligned features. We unify these threads: does query-efficient Bayesian optimization directly in an interpretable SAE feature space improve sample efficiency and auditability over optimizing in raw embeddings or a VAE latent? A Gaussian-process surrogate proposes points in the SAE space of a frozen ESM-2 (protein fitness) or a SMILES chemical LM (molecular properties), decodes them to activations, and generates candidates scored by in-silico oracles including a real ProteinGym/FLIP fitness assay. We compare against embedding-space BO, VAE-latent LSBO, trust-region and active-subspace BO, and genetic algorithms under matched oracle budgets. Our central causal test asks whether per-dimension monosemanticity—pre-registered and measured at fixed dimension against random rotations and PCA—drives efficiency, not dimensionality alone. We exploit interpretability two further ways: concept-prior warm-starting and faithful, human-readable design trajectories reporting which named concepts each step turned up or down, checked by counterfactual edits. The concrete payoff is fewer wet-lab constructs per hit for a protein engineer, plus an auditable rationale. We expect interpretable-feature BO to match or beat baselines on regret-at-budget while uniquely yielding controllable, auditable design paths—turning interpretability from a descriptive luxury into an optimization asset.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Encoders (frozen): for proteins, ESM-2 150M/650M with a TopK SAE (k=32, dictionary 16,384) on the residual stream at the intrinsic-dimension-elbow layer; for molecules, a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~10M) with a residual-stream SAE. Encoding: object -> foundation-model activations -> SAE feature vector (mean-pooled). Decoding: SAE feature vector -> reconstructed activations -> object (masked infilling / activation-conditioned decoding for proteins; activation steering during autoregressive decoding for SMILES). Encode-decode round-trip fidelity (property-preservation rate on a held-out set) is verified and reported before optimization. Oracles (cheap): proteins - ESMFold pLDDT (validity), DSSP secondary-structure targets, GRAVY, molecular weight, a thermostability/fitness head, and FLIP/ProteinGym fitness tasks where available; molecules - RDKit logP, QED, penalized-logP, docking against one fixed target, synthetic accessibility. Every reported optimization run uses >= 20 random seeds. MONOSEMANTICITY (pre-registered before optimization): per-space score = mean over active dimensions of (concept-correlation of the dimension with its best-matching labeled concept) x (activation sparsity, the fraction of inputs on which the dimension is inactive); higher means each axis carries one clean concept. Real-benchmark anchor: at least one protein setting uses a published ProteinGym/FLIP fitness assay as the oracle (not a synthetic proxy), so efficiency gains are demonstrated on a real measured landscape.

Experiment 1 (H1 - SAE-space BO is more sample-efficient): Tests whether Bayesian optimization over the SAE feature space finds better designs per oracle call than BO over raw embeddings or a VAE latent. Decisive metric: oracle-calls-to-threshold (calls to first reach a fixed target property value), median over >= 20 seeds and multiple target properties; secondary regret-at-budget. Convincing result: SAE-space BO needs >= 30% fewer oracle calls than the best competing space, with the paired 95% CI excluding a tie. Decision band: reduction in [10%, 30%] -> a real but modest efficiency gain. Negative result (< 10% or slower) refutes H1. Systems, identical GP+Expected-Improvement (qEI for batches) and identical oracle budget: (a) SAE feature space, (b) raw foundation-model embeddings PCA-reduced to the SAE's active dimension (isolating space identity from dimension), (c) a task-trained VAE latent (LaMBO-style), (d) a discrete genetic algorithm on the object; and, to show the space effect is not tied to one optimizer, each space is additionally run with trust-region BO (TuRBO), active-subspace BO, and a random-feature-map GP. Validity retention along the trajectory and novelty/diversity of optima also reported.

Experiment 2 (H3 - monosemanticity, not dimensionality, drives efficiency): Tests the central claim by holding dimensionality fixed and varying only per-axis meaning. Decisive metric: Spearman rho between a per-space monosemanticity score (mean per-feature concept-correlation / activation sparsity) and optimization efficiency (area over the regret curve), across matched-dimension spaces and target properties. Convincing result: rho >= 0.5 at fixed dimension. Decision band: rho in [0.3, 0.5] -> suggestive. Negative result (rho within [-0.2, 0.2]) means dimensionality, not monosemanticity, was doing the work, refuting H3. Matched-dimension spaces: (i) SAE features (high monosemanticity), (ii) a random rotation of the SAE basis (same geometry/dimension, meaning destroyed), (iii) PCA components (dense, mixed), (iv) a partially trained/entangled SAE. Confounder controls: results hold or covary decoder reconstruction quality, local landscape smoothness (fitted GP lengthscale), SAE sparsity level k, and active dimensionality across spaces, so monosemanticity is not a proxy for any of them.

Experiment 3 (H4 - concept-prior warm-starting cuts oracle calls, only in the interpretable space): Tests whether known feature-property associations can warm-start the search. Decisive metric: oracle-calls-to-threshold, warm-start vs cold-start, in the SAE space. Convincing result: >= 25% fewer calls warm vs cold, and the baseline spaces (which lack named axes) cannot be warm-started the same way. Decision band: reduction in [10%, 25%] -> modest speedup. Negative result (no warm-start benefit) refutes H4. Warm-start initializes the GP prior mean / restricts the initial design region using concept-correlation associations; reported with and without label filtering to expose sensitivity to noisy labels.

Experiment 4 (H2 - auditable, faithful design rationales): Tests whether the interpretable space yields human-readable rationales that are actually faithful. Decisive metric: trajectory-faithfulness score = fraction of reported concept-changes whose ablation reproduces the predicted property-change direction. Convincing result: faithfulness >= 0.7, a deliverable the raw-embedding/VAE/GA baselines cannot produce at all. Decision band: faithfulness in [0.5, 0.7] -> partially trustworthy rationales. Negative result (< 0.5) means the rationales are post-hoc and unreliable, refuting the auditability claim. Each accepted BO step emits the top named concepts increased/decreased (annotation- or LLM-labeled) and the resulting property change. Beyond ablation, faithfulness is cross-checked by a counterfactual test—constructing objects with the named concept explicitly edited and confirming the property moves as predicted—and a small decision-usefulness check asking whether an annotator, given the rationale, picks the better of two candidates above chance. The full protocol is repeated across both domains and two model sizes for robustness.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) In-silico oracles are proxies for wet-lab function; claims concern sample-efficiency and auditability of optimization, not experimental validation. 2) SAE encode/decode round-trip fidelity may be lossy, capping achievable optima; we quantify reconstruction quality and report its correlation with performance, and use the best available SAE architecture. 3) The interpretable space could win merely by favorable dimensionality; the matched-dimension monosemanticity experiment (Experiment 2) is specifically designed to rule this out. 4) GP surrogates scale poorly to very high feature dimensions; we mitigate with sparsity-aware feature selection (optimize only over active/relevant features) and additive/trust-region GPs, reporting sensitivity to this choice. 5) Concept-prior warm-starting depends on the quality of feature-property labels, which may be noisy; we report warm-start gains with and without label filtering. 6) If interpretable-feature BO merely ties baselines on regret, the auditability and warm-start results still constitute a meaningful, publishable contribution establishing interpretability as a 'free' optimization asset.

Name: causal_correlational_discrepancy
Title: When the Model Disagrees with the Textbook: Using Interpretable-Feature Interventions to Discover Causal Structure-Property Rules That Contradict Correlational Biophysics
Short Hypothesis: Framed as discrepancy-as-discovery: sparse-autoencoder features of scientific foundation models encode two kinds of structure-property associations—those that merely reflect training-data correlations and those the model uses causally during generation—and the DISAGREEMENTS between them are a hypothesis-generation engine for design rules, not just an auditing signal. By contrasting a feature's CORRELATIONAL association with a property (co-occurrence) against its CAUSAL effect (property change of the generated object when the feature is clamped), we systematically surface DISCREPANT features: an established correlational structure-property rule the model does not causally exploit (candidate spurious), or a causal rule with no catalogued correlational basis (candidate novel). We hypothesize such discrepancies are numerous, are enriched for genuinely confounded/non-causal rules when validated against independent physics-based counterfactuals, and yield candidate causal design rules that outperform correlational-only rules as steering levers.
Related Work: Two lines are relevant. (1) SAE feature discovery in scientific models (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; 'From Mechanistic Interpretability to Mechanistic Biology' 2025; the chemistry-LM SAE 2025; motif-gated domain-recognition causal patching 2025) shows features correlate with biological/chemical concepts and that some are causally necessary for a PREDICTION task. (2) Latent causal discovery (PerturbLearn attribute graphs 2022; active causal ML for molecules 2024) extracts causal graphs among attributes. Crucially, all discovery work either (a) reports concept-CORRELATION of features, or (b) verifies causal effect for a single prediction task, but NO work systematically contrasts a feature's correlational property-association with its causal generative effect to identify DISCREPANCIES, nor uses those discrepancies as a filter for finding structure-property rules that are correlational-but-not-causal (spurious) versus causal-but-uncatalogued (novel). Prior steering work treats agreement between correlation and causation as assumed; we treat their DISAGREEMENT as the scientific signal. This reframes interpretability from cataloguing what the model represents to auditing which structure-property rules are actually causal, and validates the model's verdicts against independent physics-based counterfactuals - a genuinely new use of feature interventions. The exact gap: prior auditing/causal-feature work diagnoses that some features are inert or causally necessary for a PREDICTION, but none MINES the systematic disagreement between correlation and causation to GENERATE new, testable structure-property hypotheses and then adjudicate them with an oracle independent of the model.
Abstract: Structure-property rules are the backbone of protein and molecular design, yet many textbook rules are correlational and may not reflect causal mechanism—so designers waste effort on heuristics that do not transfer. Scientific foundation models have absorbed enormous data and, through sparse autoencoders (SAEs), expose interpretable features linked to structural and property concepts. We use these features to audit and DISCOVER structure-property rules by contrasting two quantities per feature: its CORRELATIONAL association with a property (co-occurrence across natural objects) and its CAUSAL effect on the property of GENERATED objects when the feature is clamped. Features where these disagree—strong correlation but weak causal effect, or strong causal effect with weak correlation—are 'discrepant' and, we hypothesize, are enriched for spurious (confounded) or previously-uncatalogued causal design rules. We instantiate this on ESM-2 protein LMs and a SMILES chemistry LM with residual-stream SAEs and cheap in-silico evaluators. For each discrepant feature we emit a design-rule hypothesis and adjudicate it with a physics-based counterfactual test—matched object pairs differing only in the feature-linked structural element, scored by an oracle NOT derived from the model—to decide whether the model's causal verdict or the correlational rule is right. We report the rate and structure of discrepancies, their enrichment for known confounded rules (positive controls), whether causal-but-low-correlation features steer new designs where correlational rules fail, and case studies of candidate novel rules. Adopters—computational biophysicists and protein/chemical design teams—gain faster rule discovery, fewer spurious heuristics, and better candidate prioritization; the framework turns feature interventions into an auditable engine for discovering and stress-testing design rules.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (frozen): ESM-2 150M/650M with a TopK SAE (k=32, dictionary 16,384) on the residual stream (intrinsic-dimension-elbow layer) and a GPT-style SMILES chemistry LM (~10M) with a residual-stream SAE; a Matryoshka SAE variant for robustness. SAEs trained on 20M activation-tokens from 500k-object subsets, 3 SAE seeds. Feature bank: interpretable, property-linked features selected by concept-correlation/probe AUROC on held-out natural objects. Cheap evaluators on FINISHED objects: proteins - alpha-helix/beta-sheet % (DSSP on ESMFold), GRAVY, molecular weight, a thermostability proxy (light fine-tuned head), motif presence (HMMER/regex); molecules - RDKit logP, QED, ring/aromatic counts, specific functional groups (SMARTS). For each (feature, property) pair: a Correlational score (point-biserial / mutual information between feature activation and property over a large natural sample) and a Causal score (property change per unit steer at low strength within the validity budget, from a strength sweep with unsteered and norm-matched random-direction controls; validity gated by pseudo-perplexity/pLDDT or RDKit-validity). Stability controls: discrepancy calls are tested for robustness to SAE feature split/merge instability by re-deriving both scores across 3 SAE seeds and the Matryoshka variant and reporting only discrepancies stable across seeds; a probe-based association is reported alongside concept-correlation as an alternative correlational measure, and random-direction features supply a null discrepancy rate. Generation seeds: 5.

Experiment 1 (H1 - discrepant features are numerous): Tests whether plotting correlational vs causal score surfaces many features where the two disagree. Decisive metric: discrepancy rate = fraction of (feature, property) pairs whose residual from the correlation=causation diagonal exceeds a noise band set by test-retest variance of the two scores. Convincing result: discrepancy rate >= 15% of pairs, with the off-diagonal mass beyond the noise band. Decision band: discrepancy rate in [5%, 15%] -> discrepancies exist but are uncommon. Negative result (< 5%, i.e. correlation tracks causation) is itself valuable, establishing that interpretable features faithfully track causal design rules, and refutes H1. Quadrants reported: (A) high-corr/low-causal (candidate spurious), (B) low-corr/high-causal (candidate uncatalogued causal), (C) concordant; rates broken out per domain, model size, SAE variant.

Experiment 2 (H2 - discrepancies are enriched for genuinely non-causal rules): Tests whether the discrepancy map recovers KNOWN spurious rules and whether an independent physics oracle sides with the model over the textbook on adjudicated cases. Decisive metric: agreement rate between the model's causal verdict and an independent physics adjudication on a sample of discrepant pairs. Convincing result: the discrepancy filter attains precision >= 0.7 on a labeled set (known-spurious rules landing in quadrant A, known-causal in C), AND physics adjudication agrees with the model's causal verdict on >= 70% of adjudicated discrepancies. Decision band: precision or agreement in [0.5, 0.7] -> partial validation. Negative result (near-chance precision/agreement) refutes H2. Data: a literature-curated set of known confounded and known causal structure-property associations (as many as the literature supports across both domains); matched counterfactual object pairs differing only in the feature-linked structural element (single-motif insert/delete or point substitutions for proteins; minimal SMARTS edits with matched scaffolds for molecules); the adjudication oracle (FoldX/Rosetta or MD-lite for proteins; RDKit/empirical logP or docking for molecules) is deliberately independent of the generative model's training signal; matching quality reported.

Experiment 3 (H3 - discrepancies are a design-rule engine): Tests whether quadrant-B causal-but-low-correlation features act as design levers where correlational-only rules fail. Decisive metric: success rate of producing the target property in NEW designs when steering the causal (quadrant-B) feature versus applying the correlational-only rule. Convincing result: causal-rule success >= 2x correlational-only success and >= 0.10 absolute. Decision band: causal-rule success between 1.2x and 2x correlational-only -> a real but modest advantage. Negative result (causal rules no better than correlational) refutes H3. Auto-generated human-readable candidate rules (feature label + measured causal effect) are the deliverable; robustness reported across two model sizes, two SAE architectures, and both domains.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) In-silico correlational and causal scores and physics adjudicators are all imperfect proxies; the strongest claim is triangulated agreement/disagreement among independent in-silico signals, not wet-lab truth. To reduce circularity, the adjudication oracle is deliberately chosen to be independent of the generative model's training signal. 2) Discrepancies could arise from SAE artifacts (entangled features, poor reconstruction) rather than genuine causal/correlational structure; we mitigate with multiple SAE architectures, probe verification, and random-direction controls. 3) Constructing clean matched counterfactuals is hard, especially for proteins where a single edit can change many things; we restrict to minimal, well-controlled edits and report matching quality. 4) The positive-control set of known spurious/causal rules may be small, limiting enrichment power; we include as many labeled rules as the literature supports across both domains. 5) A feature's causal score depends on layer/strength; we sweep strength within the validity budget and test layer sensitivity. 6) If discrepancies turn out to be rare (correlation almost always matches causation), that is itself a valuable, publishable result establishing that interpretable features faithfully track causal design rules.

Name: cell_identity_vs_response_steering
Title: Identity Is Easy, Response Is Hard: Can Interpretable Features Causally Steer Perturbation Response in Single-Cell Foundation Models, or Only Cell-Type Identity?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable sparse-autoencoder features of single-cell foundation models (scGPT/Geneformer/scFoundation) afford steerable control over a cell's categorical IDENTITY (cell type, tissue, cell-cycle phase), but we hypothesize NOT over its DIRECTIONAL PERTURBATION RESPONSE—the signed differentially-expressed-gene (DEG) shift a specific gene knockdown/activation induces. We frame four typed contributions: (1) a contrastive identity-vs-response controllability test; (2) a response-blind-spot phenomenon—steering toward a target response reliably shifts identity while failing to reproduce the correct DEG direction; (3) a signed-DEG oracle from held-out Perturb-seq; and (4) an internal response-consistency audit. We frame results as model-internal controllability of representations rather than causal biology, and define a 'response feature' minimally as one whose steering moves the signed-DEG direction beyond what its identity shift alone explains—distinguishing it from an identity proxy. Response control is scoped as decodable-but-weakly-steerable under tested interventions, not universally absent.
Related Work: Two threads meet here for the first time. (1) SAE interpretability of single-cell foundation models (scFMs) is nascent but active: scFeatureLens/'Can SAEs make sense of gene expression LVMs' (2024) and 'SAEs Reveal Interpretable Features in scFMs' (2025) show SAE features steer cells into desired biological PROGRAMS/cell-type identities and are causally intervenable; 'Discovering Interpretable Biological Concepts in scRNA-seq FMs' (2025) and transcoder-circuit work (2025) map features/circuits to cell types and pathways. ALL of these steer toward or interpret IDENTITY/program concepts and evaluate whether a cell-type/program appears. (2) A distinct, damning benchmarking literature shows scFMs are BAD at causal perturbation response: Kendiukhov (2026) shows scFM attention 'captures co-expression rather than unique regulatory signal' and causal ablation of regulatory heads does not degrade perturbation prediction; multiple benchmarks (2025) show simple mean-baselines beat scGPT/scFoundation at post-perturbation RNA-seq prediction. NO prior work connects these: none asks whether the interpretable, steerable IDENTITY features that scFM-SAE work celebrates extend to causally controlling directional PERTURBATION RESPONSE, none contrasts identity-steerability against response-steerability, and none surfaces/audits the phenomenon that steering toward a response silently changes identity. This introduces the correlational-identity vs causal-response axis into interpretability-of-generation for a new object class (cells), is distinct from all my prior protein/molecule/DNA/RNA/reaction/crystal proposals, and is high-stakes because in-silico perturbation screening is the headline promised application of scFMs (drug/target discovery). Closest-prior contrast: [scFM SAE steering] scFeatureLens 2024 / SAEs-in-scFMs 2025 / concept-discovery 2025—steer/interpret IDENTITY or program concepts, evaluate whether a cell type/program appears; [perturbation-prediction benchmarks] Kendiukhov 2026, CellxPert/GEARS-style baselines 2025—show scFMs capture co-expression and are beaten by mean-baselines at post-perturbation prediction, but never via feature steering; [THIS proposal] contrastive identity-vs-response STEERING with a signed-DEG oracle and an internal audit. Primary novelty is a new empirical FINDING (identity steerable, response not) plus a new EVALUATION TASK/oracle (signed-DEG steering-match), not a mechanistic theory. The signed-DEG oracle could be adopted as a benchmark by the scFM/perturbation-modeling community (Perturb-seq benchmarking, GEARS/CellxPert users), beyond the scFM-interpretability niche. So-what: teams should STOP citing identity-program steering as evidence of causal perturbation control, START reporting directional DEG-match, and use the audit as a pre-wet-lab screen; concretely, identity-steering that looks like response control yields costly false positives in target discovery.
Abstract: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) are promoted for in-silico perturbation screening—predicting how a cell's transcriptome shifts under a gene knockdown or activation—a task that could accelerate drug and target discovery. Interpretability work shows sparse-autoencoder (SAE) features of scFMs are interpretable and steerable, but every demonstrated target is a categorical IDENTITY concept; separately, benchmarks find scFMs capture co-expression rather than causal regulatory signal. We unite these threads with four typed contributions: (1) a contrastive test of identity- vs response-steerability; (2) a response-blind-spot phenomenon—steering toward a target perturbation response reliably shifts cell IDENTITY while failing to reproduce the correct differentially-expressed-gene (DEG) direction; (3) a signed-DEG oracle built from held-out Perturb-seq ground truth; and (4) an internal response-consistency audit. We define a 'response feature' minimally as one whose steering moves the signed-DEG direction beyond what its identity shift alone explains. Using scGPT/Geneformer with SAEs, we LOCATE identity and response features, CAUSALLY contrast their controllability (does the steered cell's DEG signature match the true perturbation's direction and specificity?), interpret whether response units are genuine or identity proxies, and audit reliability. The concrete stake: identity-steering that masquerades as response control produces costly false positives in target discovery. Either result matters—a working response handle would be a surprising, high-value capability; a clean negative, replicated across models, datasets, and intervention types, tells the field to stop reporting identity-program success as evidence of causal perturbation control and to screen with a directional DEG oracle before wet-lab validation.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (open, FROZEN): scGPT (~50M) and Geneformer single-cell foundation models (optionally scFoundation). Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka SAEs on residual-stream activations at a late layer (richest biological programs) with strong L1, expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations, seeds 0/1/2, verified by reconstruction R^2 and L0. IDENTITY oracle: cell-type/tissue/cell-cycle-phase classifiers (linear probes on held-out Tabula Sapiens cells). RESPONSE oracle (directional causal ground truth): held-out Perturb-seq atlases - Replogle K562 (~2,057 perturbations) and RPE1 (~1,973), Norman combinatorial (~284 pairs) - each giving a perturbation's true SIGNED differentially-expressed-gene (DEG) signature. Core claims use a held-out subset of ~200 high-signal perturbations (strong, reproducible DEG sets). Response-match metrics: DEG-direction cosine / signed-rank correlation between a steered cell's induced shift and the true DEG vector, and specificity = match to the intended perturbation minus the best-matching DECOY. First confirm the models span a meaningful response RANGE. Steering = add alpha*d_hat on control cells; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - cell-IDENTITY features are causally steerable): Identify identity features (predict cell type/tissue/phase; probe AUROC) and steer a control cell to switch cell type. Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: identity-switch success rate (target-type classifier accepts the steered cell). Decision band: success >= 0.60 AND >= 0.40 over control for >=2/3 of target types => identity control genuine (H1 holds, replicating prior scFM-SAE steering); [0.15,0.40) over control => inconclusive; < 0.15 => identity not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - directional perturbation RESPONSE is decodable-but-not-steerable, and steering it silently shifts cell identity instead): (a) DECODABILITY: probe a specific perturbation's DEG-direction signature, controlling for baseline identity via partial correlation / identity-matched cells; AUROC/R^2 (critically test whether response is decodable at all independent of identity). (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: steer the best response direction (TopK/Ordered SAE feature, difference-of-means perturbed-minus-control, activation-patching from truly-perturbed cells, identity-orthogonalized direction) on control cells, decode the transcriptome shift, and compare against the model's native in-silico perturbation (gene-token deletion). Decisive metrics FIRST: SILENT-MISRESPONSE RATE = fraction of response-steered, valid cells whose decoded DEG-direction cosine to the intended perturbation < 0.20 (or matches a decoy better) while identity/validity checks pass; LEAKAGE FRACTION = share of steering displacement landing on the identity axis rather than the response axis; ratio r = response efficacy / identity efficacy from Experiment 1. Decision band: r <= 0.33 AND misresponse >= 0.30 AND leakage >= 0.60 => response blind spot confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial (test Ordered SAEs); r >= 0.67 => a genuine directional-response handle exists, refuting H2 (a surprising counter to the benchmarking literature).

Experiment 3 (H3 - identity-classification checks miss the failure but a directional DEG oracle exposes it): For the Experiment-2 cells, Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between output-side checks (identity-classifier confidence, reconstruction error, embedding plausibility) and the true DEG-direction response-match. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 => identity checks are blind while the DEG oracle exposes the wrong response (H3 confirmed); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; |rho| >= 0.40 => identity checks already reveal it (weakens the blind-spot framing). ROBUSTNESS: scGPT vs Geneformer, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, single- vs double-gene perturbations, K562 vs RPE1; test whether response steerability is worse for weak-DEG-signal and combinatorial perturbations; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.

OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS (pre-registered, with 95% CIs by bootstrap over cells/perturbations). IDENTITY AXIS = span of identity-classifier probe directions; RESPONSE AXIS = the signed-DEG direction of the target perturbation; LEAKAGE FRACTION = ||proj of steering displacement onto identity axis|| / ||total displacement||; a 'response feature' must move the response axis beyond what its identity shift alone predicts (partial effect > 0, CI excludes 0). BASELINES beyond SAE steering: raw-activation linear directions, PCA/PLS directions, CCA/mean-difference perturbation directions, and non-interpretable latent steering. SANITY GATE: on the ~200 high-signal perturbations, verify each base model's NATIVE in-silico perturbation output beats a mean/trivial baseline at DEG-direction match; if not, response non-steerability is uninterpretable and reported as such. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: shuffled-DEG signatures, decoy-perturbation matching, and cross-cell-type transfer tests to ensure the oracle is not capturing generic stress or identity drift. STRENGTHENED DISSOCIATION: construct matched examples where similar identities have DIFFERENT responses and different identities share a response. PER-ARCHITECTURE DECODING: specify how a steered activation is decoded to an expression shift for scGPT vs Geneformer, with architecture-specific sanity checks separating decoding failure from representation failure; activation patching is the architecture-agnostic cross-check. STATISTICS: report effect sizes with CIs and power across seeds/perturbations. MINIMUM CONTRIBUTION BAR: a clean negative counts if replicated across >=2 models, >=2 datasets, and >=2 intervention types.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The directional-response oracle relies on Perturb-seq data known to have low perturbation-specific variance and noisy DEG signatures; we mitigate by focusing core claims on high-signal perturbations (strong, reproducible DEG sets), using signed-rank/cosine metrics robust to noise, and reporting results stratified by native DEG-signal strength. Claims concern model-internal, in-silico-oracle-verified response controllability, not wet-lab causal biology—stated explicitly. 2) The response-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK/Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching from truly-perturbed cells, identity-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span a response range, and head-to-head calibrating that IDENTITY features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null response result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable directional-response handle) is equally publishable and would be a strong, surprising counter to the benchmarking literature. 3) Identity and response are partly entangled (a perturbation can shift a cell toward another state); the partial-correlation feature selection and identity-matched dissociation pairs (step 5) isolate genuinely identity-independent response signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) scFM benchmarks show these models barely beat trivial baselines at perturbation prediction; if response steering fails, one interpretation is 'the model has no causal response representation to steer'—which is precisely the informative, publishable finding, and the identity-steering calibration rules out that the whole pipeline is broken. 5) SAE quality/layer/regularization strongly affects biological interpretability in scFMs (needs strong L1); we control with multiple SAE variants, layers, tuned sparsity, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) An internal response-consistency probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (identity-steerable, response-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit/screening-saving payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) Decoding a steered activation back to a full transcriptome shift depends on the scFM's generative/reconstruction pathway, which differs across architectures; we standardize the DEG-direction evaluation on the decoded expression shift and use activation patching as an architecture-agnostic cross-check.
